name: Yik Oi Huang Peace and Friendship Park

facts.text: Formerly Visitacion Valley Playground; renamed in 2022 to honor community advocate Yik Oi Huang.
Has a playground, basketball court, baseball diamond, multipurpose field and a clubhouse.
Part of Candlestick Point State Recreation Area, restored as a Living Shoreline wetland for birds and wildlife.
Has lit artificial turf soccer and softball fields, a baseball diamond, tennis and basketball courts, and a playground.
Home of Bayview United Soccer Club, described as the city's first primarily Black youth soccer team.
Home to San Francisco State soccer and track and field, with a natural grass playing surface.
The track was resurfaced in 2019 and the bleachers were upgraded in 2022.

name: 101 Music
note: Chronicle article says Grant Ave store stayed open when the Green St store closed; article is older.

facts.text: The Grant Avenue store has operated since 1985; a second store on Green Street closed after 24 years.
The building was a gay bathhouse until a 1984 city order shut it down, then became the dance club Das Klub in 1986.
Reopened as 1015 Folsom in 1989, days before the Loma Prieta earthquake.
An art gallery and event space that holds art exhibitions and has two bars.
Won Best Art Gallery from SF Weekly in 2018 and 2019.

name: 15 Romolo
note: Closed for renovation since 2024; SF Standard (Jan 2026 article, Oct 2026 update) says it is reopening, so not permanently closed.

facts.text: Occupies a building that was once a brothel and later a boarding house called the Basque Hotel.
A wine bar in a space that was once a punk record shop.

name: 21st Amendment Brewery
note: SFGate (shutdown after 25 years) and Beer Street Journal say the original Second Street brewpub and the San Leandro plant closed; New School Beer (Apr 2026) only says beers are being distributed by Evil Genius, not that the brewpub reopened.

facts.text: A dive bar with original leather booths and a jukebox of rock and country classics.

name: 540 Club
note: Yelp lists 540 Club as closed (Mar 2026), but the bar continues at 540 Clement under new owners as 540 Rogues / 540 Bar; treated as a rename, not a closure.

facts.text: Four of its former bartenders bought the bar and kept it open.
Formerly called Public House; a pub with a direct entrance into Oracle Park, open on gamedays only.
Has an 8,000-square-foot rooftop-style garden patio.
Opened by bartender friends; its cocktails are made fresh rather than pre-batched.
Everyone on staff, including servers and food runners, works as a bartender.
Opened in 2005.
Home bar of the Bay Area Badgers, a Wisconsin Badgers fan group.
Founded in 1989 by Andrew McKinley at 3166 16th Street.
Became a worker-owned cooperative and moved to 24th Street in 2013 after a rent increase on 16th Street.
Its Backroom Gallery opened in 2001 in a former storage room.

name: After Hours SF
note: Yelp title: AFTER HOURS - CLOSED, 3044 Taraval St (sports bar); address now hosts After Hours Ramen / Cafe.

facts.text: Opened by the Back of the House restaurant group as a 1990s throwback bar.

name: AJ's Bar
